\text{ the rescaled solutions }\left. {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\right\}  \text{ . }
\]

We first claim that there is a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) which converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a smooth limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) on the maximal time interval \( \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Indeed, let \( {t}_{\ell } \) be a sequence of positive numbers such that \( {t}_{\ell } \rightarrow  {t}_{\max } \) and there exist smooth limits \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\ell }^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) defined on \( \left( {-{t}_{\ell },0}\right\rbrack \) . For each \( \ell \) , the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature and has bounded curvature at each time slice. Moreover by the gradient estimate in canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter \( {2\varepsilon } \) , the limit has bounded curvature on each subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left( {-{t}_{\ell },0}\right\rbrack \) . Denote by \( \widetilde{Q} \) the scalar curvature upper bound of the limit at time zero \( \left( {\widetilde{Q}\text{ is independent of }}\right. \ell ) \) . Then we can apply Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5) to get

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\ell }^{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{{t}_{\ell }}{t + {t}_{\ell }}\widetilde{Q}
\]

where \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\ell }^{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right) \) are the scalar curvatures of the limits \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\ell }^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) . Hence by the definition of convergence and the above curvature estimates, we can find a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) which converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a smooth limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) on the maximal time interval \( \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

We need to show \( - {t}_{\max } =  - \infty \) . Suppose \( - {t}_{\max } >  - \infty \) , there are only the following two possibilities: either

(1) The curvature of the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) becomes unbounded as \( t \searrow   - {t}_{\max } \) ; or

(2) For each small constant \( \theta  > 0 \) and each large integer \( {k}_{0} > 0 \) , there is some \( k \geq \; {k}_{0} \) such that the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) has a surgery time \( {T}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \theta ,0}\right\rbrack \) and a surgery point \( {x}_{k} \) lying in a gluing cap at the times \( {T}_{k} \) so that \( {d}_{{T}_{k}}^{2}\left( {{x}_{k},\bar{x}}\right) \) is uniformly bounded from above by a constant independent of \( \theta \) and \( {k}_{0} \) .

We next claim that the possibility (1) always occurs. Suppose not; then the curvature of the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is bounded on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) by some positive constant \( \widehat{C} \) . In particular, for any \( A > 0 \) , there is a sufficiently large integer \( {k}_{1} > 0 \) such that any rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) with \( k \geq  {k}_{1} \) on the geodesic ball \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and its scalar curvature is bounded by \( 2\widehat{C} \) there. (Here, without loss of generality, we may assume that the upper bound \( \widehat{C} \) is so large that \( - {t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1} < 0 \) .) By Assertion 1 in Step 2, for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) can be defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and has the scalar curvature \( \widetilde{R} \leq  {10}\widehat{C} \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . So we can extract a smooth limit from the sequence to get the limiting solution which is defined on a larger time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1}{\widehat{C}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . This contradicts the definition of the maximal time \( - {t}_{\max } \) .

It remains to exclude the possibility (1).

By using Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5) again, we have

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{{t}_{\max }}{t + {t}_{\max }}\widetilde{Q}.
\]

So we only need to control the curvature near \( - {t}_{\max } \) . Exactly as in Step 4 in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1, it follows from Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality that

(7.4.16)

\[
{\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  + {30}{t}_{\max }\sqrt{\widetilde{Q}}
\]

for any \( x, y \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and \( t \in  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Since the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time, we have some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and some time \( - {t}_{\max } < {t}_{\infty } <  - {t}_{\max } + \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1} \) such that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty }}\right)  < \; 5/4 \) . By (7.4.16), there is a constant \( {\widetilde{A}}_{0} > 0 \) such that \( {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{\infty }}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{A}}_{0}/2 \) for all \( t \in  \left( {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Now we come back to the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) . Clearly, for arbitrarily given small \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) , when \( k \) large enough, there is a point \( {y}_{k} \) in the underlying manifold of \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) at time 0 satisfying the following properties

(7.4.17)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{k},{t}_{\infty }}\right)  < \frac{3}{2},\;{\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  {\widetilde{A}}_{0}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . By the definition of convergence, we know that for any fixed \( {A}_{0} \geq  2{\widetilde{A}}_{0} \) , for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solution over \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{A}_{0}}\right) \) is defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \frac{2{t}_{\max }}{t + {t}_{\max }}\widetilde{Q}
\]

on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{A}_{0}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) . Then by Assertion 2 of Step 2, we have proved that there is a sufficiently large integer \( {\bar{k}}_{0} \) such that when \( k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0} \) , the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) at \( {y}_{k} \) can be defined on \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) , and satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  {15}
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) .

We now prove a statement analogous to Assertion 4 (i) of Step 3.

Assertion 5. For the above rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) and \( {\bar{k}}_{0} \) , we have that for any \( L > 0 \) , there is a positive constant \( \omega \left( L\right) \) such that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \omega \left( L\right)
\]

for all \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x,{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  L \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) , and for all \( k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0} \) .

Proof of Assertion 5. We slightly modify the argument in the proof of Assertion 4 (i). Let

\[
M\left( \rho \right)  = \sup \left\{  {\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  {\widetilde{d}}_{t}\left( {x,{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  \rho }\right. \text{ and }t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
\text{ in the rescaled solutions }\left. {{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}, k \geq  {\bar{k}}_{0}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \sup \{ \rho  > 0 \mid  M\left( \rho \right)  <  + \infty \} .
\]

Note that the estimate (7.4.14) implies that \( {\rho }_{0} > 0 \) . We only need to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) .

We argue by contradiction. Suppose \( {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) . Then, after passing to a subsequence, there is a sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{y}}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) in the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) with \( {t}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{50}{\eta }^{-1},{t}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) and \( {\widetilde{d}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\widetilde{y}}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) such that \( \widetilde{R}\left( {{\widetilde{y}}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Denote by \( {\gamma }_{k} \) a minimizing geodesic segment from \( {y}_{k} \) to \( {\widetilde{y}}_{k} \) at the time \( {t}_{k} \) and denote by \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\rho }_{0}}\right) \) the open geodesic ball centered at \( {y}_{k} \) of radius \( {\rho }_{0} \) on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) \) .

For any \( 0 < \rho  < {\rho }_{0} \) with \( \rho \) near \( {\rho }_{0} \) , by applying Assertion 3 as before, we get that the rescaled solutions on the balls \( {B}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},\rho }\right) \) are defined on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}M{\left( \rho \right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) for all large \( k \) . By Step 1 and Shi’s derivative estimate, we further know that the covariant derivatives and higher order derivatives of the curvatures on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},\rho  - \frac{\left( {\rho }_{0} - \rho \right) }{2}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - \frac{1}{32}{\eta }^{-1}M{\left( \rho \right) }^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) are also uniformly bounded. Then by the uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), after passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the marked sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{B}}_{{t}_{k}}\left( {{y}_{k},{\rho }_{0}}\right) ,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}}\left( {\cdot ,{t}_{k}}\right) ,{y}_{k}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a marked (noncomplete) manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{y}_{\infty }}\right) \) and the geodesic segments \( {\gamma }_{k} \) converge to a geodesic segment (missing an endpoint) \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) emanating from \( {y}_{\infty } \) .

Clearly, the limit also has nonnegative sectional curvature by the pinching assumption. Then by repeating the same argument as in the proof of Assertion 4 (i) in the rest, we derive a contradiction with Hamilton's strong maximum principle. This proves Assertion 5.

We then apply the second estimate of (7.4.17) and Assertion 5 to conclude that for any large constant \( 0 < A <  + \infty \) , there is a positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) such that for any small \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) , the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) satisfy

(7.4.18)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) , and for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Then by applying Assertion 1 in Step 2, we conclude that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) on the geodesic balls \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) are also defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime } - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) for all sufficiently large \( k \) . Furthermore, by the gradient estimates as in Step 1, we have

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}\left( A\right)
\]

for \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } + {\epsilon }^{\prime } - \frac{1}{8}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) . Since \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } > 0 \) is arbitrarily small and the positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) is independent of \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } \) , we conclude that the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) on \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) are defined on the extended time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - }\right. \; \left. {\frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) and satisfy

(7.4.19)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {10C}\left( A\right) ,
\]

for \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max } - \frac{1}{16}{\eta }^{-1}C{\left( A\right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) , and for all sufficiently large \( k \) .

Now, by taking convergent subsequences from the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{k}{\beta }_{k}} \) , we see that the limit solution is defined smoothly on a space-time open subset of \( {M}_{\infty } \times \; ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) containing \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) . By Step 4, we see that the limiting metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }\left( {\cdot , - {t}_{\max }}\right) \) at time \( - {t}_{\max } \) has bounded curvature. Then by combining with the canonical neighborhood assumption of accuracy \( {2\varepsilon } \) , we conclude that the curvature of the limit is uniformly bounded on the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-{t}_{\max },0}\right\rbrack \) . So we have excluded the possibility (1).

Hence we have proved a subsequence of the rescaled solutions converges to an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution.

Finally by combining with the canonical neighborhood theorem (Theorem 6.4.6), we see that \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) has a canonical neighborhood with parameter \( \varepsilon \) , which is a contradiction. Therefore we have completed the proof of the proposition. 0

Without loss of generality, we may assume \( 0 < \varepsilon  \leq  {\bar{\varepsilon }}_{0} \) , where \( {\bar{\varepsilon }}_{0} \) is the sufficiently small (universal) positive constant in Lemma 7.4.2.

By the same argument as in the first part of the proof of Lemma 7.4.2, the canonical neighborhood assumption of the solution implies the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing on the scales less than \( \frac{1}{2\eta }\widetilde{r}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) for some positive constant \( \kappa \) depending only on \( {C}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) and \( {C}_{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) (in the definition of the canonical neighborhood assumption). for those points in \( P\left( {x,{t}_{0},\rho , - {\rho }^{2}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {y, t}\right)  \mid  y \in  {B}_{t}\left( {x,\rho }\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - {\rho }^{2},{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) for which the solution is defined. We will adapt both the proof of Proposition 7.4.1 and that of Theorem 7.2.1 to show that a sequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) converges to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which will give the desired contradiction. Since we only need to consider the scale of the curvature less than \( \widetilde{r}{\left( \bar{t}\right) }^{-2} \) , the present situation is much easier than that of Proposition 7.4.1.

Firstly as before, we need to get a local curvature estimate.

For each adjusted \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , let \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) be the maximal subinterval of \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) so that for each sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and then sufficiently large \( \beta \) , the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) in \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},{t}^{\prime } - \bar{t}}\right)  = \{ \left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  x \in \; {B}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack  \} \) with \( R\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) , where \( \eta \) is the universal positive constant in the definition of canonical neighborhood assumption. We want to show

(7.5.13)

\[
{t}^{\prime } = \bar{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}.
\]

Consider the scalar curvature \( R \) at the point \( \bar{x} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . If there is a time \( \widetilde{t} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) satisfying \( R\left( {\bar{x},\widetilde{t}}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) , we let \( \widetilde{t} \) be the first of such time from \( \bar{t} \) . Since the chosen point \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) does not satisfy the canonical neighborhood statement, we know \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{r}{\left( \bar{t}\right) }^{-2} \) . Recall from our designed surgery procedure that if there is a cutoff surgery at a point \( x \) at a time \( t \) , the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is at least \( {\left( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2}\widetilde{r}{\left( t\right) }^{-2} \) . Then for each fixed \( \alpha \) , for \( \beta \) large enough, the solution \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) around the point \( \bar{x} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\widetilde{t}}\right\rbrack \) is well defined and satisfies the following curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  8\bar{Q},
\]

for \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) if there is no such time \( \widetilde{t} \) ). By the assumption that \( {t}_{0} > 2{r}_{0}^{2} \) , we have

\[
\bar{t}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {r}_{0}^{2}\left( {{K}_{1}{r}_{0}^{-2}}\right)
\]

\[
= {K}_{1} \rightarrow   + \infty \text{ . }
\]

Thus by using the pinching assumption and the gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption, we further have

\[
\left| {{Rm}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {30}\bar{Q},
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{t}\left( {\bar{x},\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) and all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Observe that Lemma 3.4.1 (ii) is applicable for \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{x}}\right) \) with \( t \in \; \left\lbrack  {\widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) since any minimal geodesic, with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) , connecting \( {x}_{0} \) and \( \bar{x} \) lies in the region unaffected by surgery; otherwise the geodesic is not minimal. After having obtained the above curvature estimate, we can argue as deriving (7.2.2) and (7.2.3) in the proof of Theorem 7.2.1 to conclude that any point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) , with \( \widetilde{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  \bar{t} \) (or \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) ) and \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , satisfies

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  \leq  {d}_{\bar{t}}\left( {\bar{x},{x}_{0}}\right)  + \frac{1}{2}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},
\]

for all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Then by combining with the choice of the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we prove \( {t}^{\prime } = \bar{t} - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1} \) (i.e., the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any point \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) with \( R\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) ) for all sufficiently large \( \alpha \) and then sufficiently large \( \beta \) .

Now it follows from the gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption that the scalar curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) satisfy

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {40}
\]

for those \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {\bar{x},\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) ,{t}^{\prime } \in  }\right. \; \left. \left\lbrack  {-\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  \right\} \) , for which the rescaled solution is defined. (Here \( {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }} \) denotes the geodesic ball in the rescaled solution at time \( {t}^{\prime } \) ). Note again that \( R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{r}{\left( \bar{t}\right) }^{-2} \) and recall from our designed surgery procedure that if there is a cutoff surgery at a point \( x \) at a time \( t \) , the scalar curvature at \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) is at least \( {\left( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2}\widetilde{r}{\left( t\right) }^{-2} \) . Then for each fixed sufficiently large \( \alpha \) , for \( \beta \) large enough, the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) is defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) \) . More generally, for arbitrarily fixed \( 0 < \widetilde{K} <  + \infty \) , there is a positive integer \( {\alpha }_{0} \) so that for each \( \alpha  \geq  {\alpha }_{0} \) we can

find \( {\beta }_{0} > 0 \) (depending on \( \alpha \) ) such that if \( \beta  \geq  {\beta }_{0} \) and \( \left( {y,0}\right) \) is a point on the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( \widetilde{R}\left( {y,0}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{K} \) and \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {y,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{K} \) , we have estimate

(7.5.14)

\[
\widetilde{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {40}\widetilde{K}
\]

for \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  P\left( {y,0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1}}\right)  \triangleq  \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{{t}^{\prime }}\left( {y,}\right) }\right. \; \left. {\left. {\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\rbrack  ,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {-\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1},0}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) . In particular, the rescaled solution is defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {y,0,\frac{1}{10}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}, - \frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}{\widetilde{K}}^{-1}}\right) \) .

Next, we want to show the curvature of the rescaled solutions at the new times zero (after shifting) stay uniformly bounded at bounded distances from \( \bar{x} \) for some subsequences of \( \alpha \) and \( \beta \) . Let \( {\alpha }_{m},{\beta }_{m} \rightarrow   + \infty \) be chosen so that the estimate (7.5.14) holds with \( \widetilde{K} = m \) . For all \( \rho  \geq  0 \) , set

\[
M\left( \rho \right)  = \sup \left\{  {\widetilde{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \mid  m \geq  1,{d}_{0}\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  \rho \text{ in the rescaled solutions }{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}}\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \sup \{ \rho  \geq  0 \mid  M\left( \rho \right)  <  + \infty \} .
\]

Clearly the estimate (7.5.14) yields \( {\rho }_{0} > 0 \) . As we consider the unshifted time \( \bar{t} \) , by combining with the assumption that \( {t}_{0} > 2{r}_{0}^{2} \) , we have

(7.5.15)

\[
\bar{t}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  \geq  \frac{{t}_{0}}{2}R\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {r}_{0}^{2}\left( {{K}_{1}{r}_{0}^{-2}}\right)
\]

\[
= {K}_{1} \rightarrow   + \infty \text{ . }
\]

It then follows from the pinching assumption that we only need to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) . As before, we argue by contradiction. Suppose we have a sequence of points \( {y}_{m} \) in the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) with \( {\widetilde{d}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{y}_{m}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) and \( \widetilde{R}\left( {{y}_{m},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Denote by \( {\gamma }_{m} \) a minimizing geodesic segment from \( \bar{x} \) to \( {y}_{m} \) and denote by \( {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{\rho }_{0}}\right) \) the open geodesic balls centered at \( \bar{x} \) of radius \( {\rho }_{0} \) of the rescaled solutions. By applying the assertion in statement (i), we have uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing at the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) . By combining with the local curvature estimate (7.5.14) and Hamilton's compactness theorem, we can assume that, after passing to a subsequence, the marked sequence \( \left( {{\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {\bar{x},{\rho }_{0}}\right) ,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}},\bar{x}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a marked (noncomplete) manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) and the geodesic segments \( {\gamma }_{m} \) converge to a geodesic segment (missing an endpoint) \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) . Moreover, by the pinching assumption and the estimate (7.5.15), the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature.

Then exactly as before, we consider the tubular neighborhood along \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \)

\[
V = \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{{q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty }}}{B}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{0},{4\pi }{\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right)
\]

and the completion \( {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) of \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) \) with \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) the limit point of \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) . As before, by the choice of the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) , we know that the limiting metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty } \) is cylindrical at any point \( {q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty } \) which is sufficiently close to \( {y}_{\infty } \) . Then by the same reason as before the metric space \( \bar{V} = V \cup  \left\{  {y}_{\infty }\right\} \) has nonnegative curvature in Alexandrov sense, and we have a three-dimensional nonflat tangent cone \( {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V} \) at \( {y}_{\infty } \) . Pick \( z \in  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V} \) with distance one from the vertex and it is nonflat around \( z \) . By definition \( B\left( {z,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \left( { \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V}}\right) \) is the Gromov-Hausdoff convergent limit of the scalings of a sequence of balls \( {B}_{\infty }\left( {{z}_{k},{\sigma }_{k}}\right) \left( { \subset  \left( {V,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) }\right) \) with \( {\sigma }_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) . Since the estimate (7.5.14) survives on \( \left( {V,{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty }}\right) \) for all \( \widetilde{K} <  + \infty \) , we know that this convergence is actually in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology and over some time interval. Since the limit \( B\left( {z,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \left( { \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{V}}\right) \) is a piece of a nonnegatively curved nonflat metric cone, we get a contradiction with Hamilton's strong maximum Principle (Theorem 2.2.1) as before. Hence we have proved that a subsequence of the rescaled solution \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) has uniformly bounded curvatures at bounded distance from \( \bar{x} \) at the new times zero.

Further, by the uniform \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing at the points \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) and the estimate (7.5.14) again, we can take a \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) , defined on a space-time subset which contains the time slice \( \{ t = 0\} \) and is relatively open in \( {M}_{\infty } \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , for the subsequence of the rescaled solutions. The limit is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow, and is complete at \( t = 0 \) , as well as has nonnegative sectional curvature by the pinching assumption and the estimate (7.5.15). Thus by repeating the same argument as in the Step 4 of the proof Proposition 7.4.1, we conclude that the curvature of the limit at \( t = 0 \) is bounded.

Finally we try to extend the limit backwards in time to get an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Since the curvature of the limit is bounded at \( t = 0 \) , it follows from the estimate (7.5.14) that the limit is a smooth solution to the Ricci flow defined at least on a backward time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-a,0}\right\rbrack \) for some positive constant \( a \) . Let \( \left( {{t}_{\infty },0}\right\rbrack \) be the maximal time interval over which we can extract a smooth limiting solution. It suffices to show \( {t}_{\infty } =  - \infty \) . If \( {t}_{\infty } >  - \infty \) , there are only two possibilities: either there exist surgeries in finite distance around the time \( {t}_{\infty } \) or the curvature of the limiting solution becomes unbounded as \( t \searrow  {t}_{\infty } \) .

Let \( c > 0 \) be a positive constant much smaller than \( \frac{1}{100}{\eta }^{-1} \) . Note again that the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time. Then we can find some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and some time \( t = {t}_{\infty } + \theta \) with \( 0 < \theta  < \frac{c}{3} \) such that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right)  \leq  2 \) .

Consider the (unrescaled) scalar curvature \( R \) of \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at the point \( \bar{x} \) over the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Since the scalar curvature \( {R}_{\infty } \) of the limit on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{3},0}\right\rbrack \) is uniformly bounded by some positive constant \( C \) , we have the curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {\bar{x}, t}\right)  \leq  {2C}\bar{Q}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) and all sufficiently large \( m \) . For each fixed \( m \) and \( {\alpha }_{m} \) , we may require the chosen \( {\beta }_{m} \) to satisfy

\[
{\left( {\bar{\delta }}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\right) }^{-2}{\left( \widetilde{r}\left( \frac{{t}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}}}{2}\right) \right) }^{-2} \geq  m\widetilde{r}{\left( {t}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}}\right) }^{-2} \geq  m\bar{Q}.
\]

When \( m \) is large enough, we observe again that Lemma 3.4.1 (ii) is applicable for \( {d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{0},\bar{x}}\right) \) with \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) . Then by repeating the argument as in the derivation of (7.2.1),(7.2.2) and (7.2.3), we deduce that for all sufficiently large \( m \) , the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{\theta }{2}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) . \)

Let \( \left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) be a sequence of associated points and times in the (unrescaled) solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) so that after rescaling, the sequence converges to \( \left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}_{\infty } + \theta }\right) \) in the limit. Clearly \( \frac{\theta }{2} \leq  {\theta }_{m} \leq  {2\theta } \) for all sufficiently large \( m \) . Then by the argument as in the derivation of (7.5.13), we know that for all sufficiently large \( m \) , the solution \( {g}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at \( {y}_{m} \) is defined on the whole time interval \( \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m} - }\right. }\right. \; \left. {\left. {\frac{1}{20}{\eta }^{-1}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + {\theta }_{m}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) and satisfies the curvature estimate

\[
R\left( {{y}_{m}, t}\right)  \leq  8\bar{Q}
\]

there; moreover the canonical neighborhood statement holds for any \( \left( {y, t}\right) \) with \( R\left( {y, t}\right)  \geq  4\bar{Q} \) in the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) .

We now consider the rescaled sequence \( {\widetilde{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) with the marked points replaced by \( {y}_{m} \) and the times replaced by \( {s}_{m} \in  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{4}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1},\bar{t} + \left( {{t}_{\infty } + \frac{c}{4}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) . As before the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality implies the rescaling limit around \( \left( {{y}_{m},{s}_{m}}\right) \) agrees with the original one. Then the arguments in previous paragraphs imply the limit is well-defined and smooth on a space-time open neighborhood of the maximal time slice \( \left\{  {t = {t}_{\infty }}\right\} \) . Particularly this excludes the possibility of existing surgeries in finite distance around the time \( {t}_{\infty } \) . Moreover, the limit at \( t = {t}_{\infty } \) also has bounded curvature. By using the gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption on the parabolic neighborhood \( P\left( {{y}_{m},\bar{t},\frac{1}{10}{K}_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\bar{Q}}^{-\frac{1}{2}},\left( {{t}_{\infty } - \frac{c}{3}}\right) {\bar{Q}}^{-1}}\right) \) , we see that the second possibility is also impossible. Hence we have proved a subsequence of the rescaled solutions converges to an ancient \( \kappa \) -solution.

Therefore we have proved the canonical neighborhood statement (ii).

(iii) This is analogous to Theorem 7.2.1. We also argue by contradiction. Suppose for some \( A <  + \infty \) and sequences of positive numbers \( {K}_{2}^{\alpha } \rightarrow   + \infty ,{\bar{r}}^{\alpha } \rightarrow  0 \) there exists a sequence of times \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \) such that for any sequences \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } > 0 \) with \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \rightarrow  0 \) for fixed \( \alpha \) , we have sequences of solutions \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) to the Ricci flow with surgery and sequences of points \( {x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) , of positive constants \( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) with \( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  {\bar{r}}^{\alpha }\sqrt{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }} \) which satisfy the assumptions, but for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) there hold

(7.5.16)

\[
R\left( {{x}^{\alpha \beta },{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\right)  > {K}_{2}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2}\text{ , for some }{x}^{\alpha \beta } \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\left( {{x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }, A{r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }}\right) .
\]

We may assume that \( {\bar{\delta }}^{\alpha \beta } \leq  {\bar{\delta }}_{4A}\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) \) for all \( \alpha ,\beta \) , where \( {\bar{\delta }}_{4A}\left( {t}_{0}^{\alpha }\right) \) is chosen so that the statements (i) and (ii) hold on \( {B}_{{t}_{0}^{\alpha }}\left( {{x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta },{4A}{r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }}\right) \) . Let \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) be the rescaled solutions of \( {g}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) around the origins \( {x}_{0}^{\alpha \beta } \) with factor \( {\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2} \) and shift the times \( {t}_{0}^{\alpha } \) to zero. Then by applying the statement (ii), we know that the regions, where the scalar curvature of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) is at least \( {K}_{1}\left( { = {K}_{1}\left( {4A}\right) }\right) \) , are canonical neighborhood regions. Note that canonical \( \varepsilon \) -neck neighborhoods are strong. Also note that the pinching assumption and the assertion

\[
{t}_{0}^{\alpha }{\left( {r}_{0}^{\alpha \beta }\right) }^{-2} \geq  {\left( {\bar{r}}^{\alpha }\right) }^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty ,\text{ as }\alpha  \rightarrow   + \infty ,
\]

imply that any subsequent limit of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{\alpha \beta } \) must have nonnegative sectional curvature. Thus by the above argument in the proof of the statement (ii) (or the argument in Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 7.1.1), we conclude that there exist subsequences \( \alpha  = {\alpha }_{m},\beta  = {\beta }_{m} \) such that the curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widehat{g}}_{ij}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) stay uniformly bounded at distances from the origins \( {x}_{0}^{{\alpha }_{m}{\beta }_{m}} \) not exceeding \( {2A} \) . This contradicts (7.5.16) for \( m \) sufficiently large. This proves the statements (iii).

Clearly for fixed \( A \) , after defining the \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) for each \( {t}_{0} \) , one can adjust the \( {\bar{\delta }}_{A}\left( {t}_{0}\right) \) so that it is nonincreasing in \( {t}_{0} \) .

Therefore we have completed the proof of the theorem.

From now on we redefine the function \( \widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right) \) so that it is also less than \( {\bar{\delta }}_{2\left( {t + 1}\right) }\left( {2t}\right) \) and then the above theorem always holds for \( A \in  \left\lbrack  {1,2\left( {{t}_{0} + 1}\right) }\right\rbrack \) . Particularly, we still

have

\[
\widetilde{\delta }\left( t\right)  \leq  \bar{\delta }\left( t\right)  = \min \left\{  {\frac{1}{2{e}^{2}\log \left( {1 + t}\right) },{\delta }_{0}}\right\}  ,
\]

which tends to zero as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) . We may also require that \( \widetilde{r}\left( t\right) \) tends to zero as \( t \rightarrow   + \infty \) .

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (Singularity structure theorem). Given \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) and \( {T}_{0} > 1 \) , one can find \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) with the following property. If \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) , x \in  M \) and \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) with \( 1 < T \leq  {T}_{0} \) , is a solution to the Ricci flow on a compact orientable three-manifold \( M \) with normalized initial metric, then for any point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) and \( Q = \; R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) , the solution in \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \mid  {d}_{{t}_{0}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  < {\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}^{-1},\;{t}_{0} - {\varepsilon }^{-2}{Q}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{0}}\right\} \) is, after scaling by the factor \( Q,\varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) -topology) to the corresponding subset of some orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution (for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) ).

Since the initial metric is normalized, it follows from the no local collapsing theorem I or I' (and their proofs) that there is a positive constant \( \kappa \) , depending only on \( {T}_{0} \) , such that the solution in Theorem 7.1.1 is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales less than \( \sqrt{{T}_{0}} \) . Let \( C\left( \varepsilon \right) \) be a positive constant larger than or equal to \( {\varepsilon }^{-2} \) . It suffices to prove that there exists \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) such that for any point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) and \( Q = \; R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) , the solution in the parabolic region \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  M\times \lbrack 0, T) \mid  {d}_{{t}_{0}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  < }\right. \; \left. {C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}^{-1},{t}_{0} - C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{0}}\right\} \) is, after scaling by the factor \( Q,\varepsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of some orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. The constant \( C\left( \varepsilon \right) \) will be determined later.

We argue by contradiction. Suppose for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) , there exist a sequence of solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) to the Ricci flow on compact orientable three-manifolds with normalized initial metrics, defined on the time intervals \( \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{k}}\right) \) with \( 1 < {T}_{k} \leq  {T}_{0} \) , a sequence of positive numbers \( {r}_{k} \rightarrow  0 \) , and a sequence of points \( {x}_{k} \in  {M}_{k} \) and times \( {t}_{k} \geq  1 \) with \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right)  \geq  {r}_{k}^{-2} \) such that each solution \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) in the parabolic region \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {M}_{k} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{k}}\right)  \mid  {d}_{{t}_{k}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  < C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k} - C\left( \varepsilon \right) {Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{k}}\right\} \) is not, after scaling by the factor \( {Q}_{k},\varepsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of any orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, where \( {R}_{k} \) denotes the scalar curvature of \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}}\right) \) .

For each solution \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) , we may adjust the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{k} \geq  \frac{1}{2} \) and with \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) to be as large as possible so that the conclusion of the theorem fails at \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , but holds for any \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {M}_{k} \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} - {H}_{k}{Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k}}\right\rbrack \) satisfying \( {R}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \geq  2{Q}_{k} \) , where \( {H}_{k} = \frac{1}{4}{r}_{k}^{-2} \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( k \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Indeed, suppose not, by setting \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{1}},{t}_{{k}_{1}}}\right)  = \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , we can choose a sequence of points \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{l}},{t}_{{k}_{l}}}\right)  \in  {M}_{k} \times \; \left\lbrack  {{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }} - {H}_{k}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }},{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }}\right) }^{-1},{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }}}\right\rbrack \) such that \( {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{l}},{t}_{{k}_{l}}}\right)  \geq  2{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }},{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }}}\right) \) and the conclusion of the theorem fails at \( \left( {{x}_{{k}_{l}},{t}_{{k}_{l}}}\right) \) for each \( l = 2,3,\ldots \) . Since the solution is smooth, but

\[
{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{l}},{t}_{{k}_{l}}}\right)  \geq  2{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }},{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }}}\right)  \geq  \cdots  \geq  {2}^{l - 1}{R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) ,
\]

\[
{t}_{{k}_{l}} \geq  {t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }} - {H}_{k}{R}_{k}{\left( {x}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }},{t}_{{k}_{\left( l - 1\right) }}\right) }^{-1}

\[

\]

this process must terminate after a finite number of steps and the last element fits.

Let \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) be the rescaled solutions obtained by rescaling \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) around \( {x}_{k} \) with the factors \( {Q}_{k} = {R}_{k}\left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) and shifting the time \( {t}_{k} \) to the new time zero. Denote by \( {\widetilde{R}}_{k} \) the rescaled scalar curvature. We will show that a subsequence of the orientable rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which is a contradiction. In the following we divide the argument into four steps.

Step 1. First of all, we need a local bound on curvatures.

Lemma 7.1.2. For each \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{k} - \frac{1}{2}{H}_{k}{Q}_{k}^{-1} \leq  \bar{t} \leq  {t}_{k} \) , we have \( {R}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4{\bar{Q}}_{k} \) whenever \( \bar{t} - c{\bar{Q}}_{k}^{-1} \leq  t \leq  \bar{t} \) and \( {d}_{\bar{t}}^{2}\left( {x,\bar{x}}\right)  \leq  c{\bar{Q}}_{k}^{-1} \) , where \( {\bar{Q}}_{k} = {Q}_{k} + {R}_{k}\left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) and \( c > 0 \) is a small universal constant.

Proof. Consider any point \( \left( {x, t}\right)  \in  {B}_{\bar{t}}\left( {\bar{x},{\left( c{\bar{Q}}_{k}^{-1}\right) }^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {\bar{t} - c{\bar{Q}}_{k}^{-1},\bar{t}}\right\rbrack \) with \( c > 0 \) to be determined. If \( {R}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  2{Q}_{k} \) , there is nothing to show. If \( {R}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  > 2{Q}_{k} \) , consider a space-time curve \( \gamma \) from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) that goes straight from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( \left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) \) and goes from \( \left( {x,\bar{t}}\right) \) to \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) along a minimizing geodesic (with respect to the metric \( {g}_{k}\left( {\cdot ,\bar{t}}\right) \) ). If there is a point on \( \gamma \) with the scalar curvature \( 2{Q}_{k} \) , let \( {y}_{0} \) be the nearest such point to \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) . If not, put \( {y}_{0} = \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right) \) . On the segment of \( \gamma \) from \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) to \( {y}_{0} \) , the scalar curvature is at least \( 2{Q}_{k} \) . According to the choice of the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , the solution along the segment is \( \varepsilon \) -close to that of some ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. It follows from Theorem 6.4.3 (ii) that

\[
\left| {\nabla \left( {R}_{k}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {2\eta }\text{ and }\left| {\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {R}_{k}^{-1}\right) }\right|  \leq  {2\eta }
\]

on the segment. (Here, without loss of generality, we may assume \( \varepsilon \) is suitably small). Then by choosing \( c > 0 \) (depending only on \( \eta \) ) small enough we get the desired curvature bound by integrating the above derivative estimates along the segment. This proves the lemma.

Step 2. Next we want to show that for each \( A <  + \infty \) , there exist a positive constant \( C\left( A\right) \) (independent of \( k \) ) such that the curvatures of the rescaled solutions

\( {\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at the new time \( t = 0 \) (corresponding to the original times \( {t}_{k} \) ) satisfy the estimate

\[
\left| \widetilde{R{m}_{k}}\right| \left( {y,0}\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)
\]

whenever \( {d}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\left( {y,{x}_{k}}\right)  \leq  A \) and \( k \geq  1 \) .

For each \( \rho  \geq  0 \) , set

\[
M\left( \rho \right)  = \sup \left\{  {{\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {x,0}\right)  \mid  k \geq  1, x \in  {M}_{k}\text{ with }{d}_{0}\left( {x,{x}_{k}}\right)  \leq  \rho }\right\}
\]

and

\[
{\rho }_{0} = \sup \{ \rho  \geq  0 \mid  M\left( \rho \right)  <  + \infty \} .
\]

By the pinching estimate (7.1.1), it suffices to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) .

Note that \( {\rho }_{0} > 0 \) by applying Lemma 7.1.2 with \( \left( {\bar{x},\bar{t}}\right)  = \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) . We now argue by contradiction to show \( {\rho }_{0} =  + \infty \) . Suppose not, we may find (after passing to a subsequence if necessary) a sequence of points \( {y}_{k} \in  {M}_{k} \) with \( {d}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k},{y}_{k}}\right)  \rightarrow  {\rho }_{0} <  + \infty \) and \( {\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {{y}_{k},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) . Let \( {\gamma }_{k}\left( { \subset  {M}_{k}}\right) \) be a minimizing geodesic segment from \( {x}_{k} \) to \( {y}_{k} \) . Let \( {z}_{k} \in  {\gamma }_{k} \) be the point on \( {\gamma }_{k} \) closest to \( {y}_{k} \) with \( {\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {{z}_{k},0}\right)  = 2 \) , and let \( {\beta }_{k} \) be the subsegment of \( {\gamma }_{k} \) running from \( {z}_{k} \) to \( {y}_{k} \) . By Lemma 7.1.2 the length of \( {\beta }_{k} \) is bounded away from zero independent of \( k \) . By the pinching estimate (7.1.1), for each \( \rho  < {\rho }_{0} \) , we have a uniform bound on the curvatures on the open balls \( {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k},\rho }\right)  \subset  \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}}\right) \) . The injectivity radii of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k} \) at the points \( {x}_{k} \) and the time \( t = 0 \) are also uniformly bounded from below by the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing property. Therefore by Lemma 7.1.2 and Hamilton's compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), after passing to a subsequence, we can assume that the marked sequence \( \left( {{B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k},{\rho }_{0}}\right) ,{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a marked (noncomplete) manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) , the segments \( {\gamma }_{k} \) converge to a geodesic segment (missing an endpoint) \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \subset  {B}_{\infty } \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) , and \( {\beta }_{k} \) converges to a subsegment \( {\beta }_{\infty } \) of \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) . Let \( {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) denote the completion of \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }}\right) \) , and \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {\bar{B}}_{\infty } \) the limit point of \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) .

Denote by \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty } \) the scalar curvature of \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }}\right) \) . Since the rescaled scalar curvatures \( {\widetilde{R}}_{k} \) along \( {\beta }_{k} \) are at least 2, it follows from the choice of the points \( \left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) that for any \( {q}_{0} \in  {\beta }_{\infty } \) , the manifold \( \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }}\right) \) in \( \left\{  {q \in  {B}_{\infty } \mid  {\operatorname{dist}}_{{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }}^{2}\left( {q,{q}_{0}}\right)  < C\left( \varepsilon \right) {\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-1}}\right\} \) is \( {2\varepsilon } \) -close to the corresponding subset of (a time slice of) some orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution. Then by Theorem 6.4.6, we know that the orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution at each point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) has a radius \( r,0 < r < {C}_{1}\left( {2\varepsilon }\right) R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , such that its canonical neighborhood \( B \) , with \( {B}_{t}\left( {x, r}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{t}\left( {x,{2r}}\right) \) , is either an evolving \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck, or an evolving \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap, or a compact manifold (without boundary) diffeomorphic to a metric quotient of the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) , and moreover the scalar curvature is between \( {\left( {C}_{2}\left( 2\varepsilon \right) \right) }^{-1}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}\left( {2\varepsilon }\right) R\left( {x, t}\right) \) , where \( {C}_{1}\left( {2\varepsilon }\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}\left( {2\varepsilon }\right) \) are the positive constants in Theorem 6.4.6.

We now choose \( C\left( \varepsilon \right)  = \max \left\{  {2{C}_{1}^{2}\left( {2\varepsilon }\right) ,{\varepsilon }^{-2}}\right\} \) . By the local curvature estimate in Lemma 7.1.2, we see that the scalar curvature \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty } \) becomes unbounded when approaching \( {y}_{\infty } \) along \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) . This implies that the canonical neighborhood around \( {q}_{0} \) cannot be a compact manifold (without boundary) diffeomorphic to a metric quotient of the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) . Note that \( {\gamma }_{\infty } \) is shortest since it is the limit of a sequence of shortest geodesics. Without loss of generality, we may assume \( \varepsilon \) is suitably small (say, \( \varepsilon  \leq  \frac{1}{100} \) ). These imply that as \( {q}_{0} \) gets sufficiently close to \( {y}_{\infty } \) , the canonical neighborhood around \( {q}_{0} \) cannot be an evolving \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap. Thus we conclude that each \( {q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty } \) sufficiently close to \( {y}_{\infty } \) is the center of an evolving \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck.

Let

\[
U = \mathop{\bigcup }\limits_{{{q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty }}}B\left( {{q}_{0},{4\pi }{\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \;\left( { \subset  \left( {{B}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }}\right) }\right) ,
\]

where \( B\left( {{q}_{0},{4\pi }{\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) is the ball centered at \( {q}_{0} \in  {B}_{\infty } \) with the radius \( {4\pi }{\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{0}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . Clearly \( U \) has nonnegative sectional curvature by the pinching estimate (7.1.1). Since the metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{\infty } \) is cylindrical at any point \( {q}_{0} \in  {\gamma }_{\infty } \) which is sufficiently close to \( {y}_{\infty } \) , we see that the metric space \( \bar{U} = U \cup  \left\{  {y}_{\infty }\right\} \) by adding in the point \( {y}_{\infty } \) , is locally complete and intrinsic near \( {y}_{\infty } \) . Furthermore \( {y}_{\infty } \) cannot be an interior point of any geodesic segment in \( \bar{U} \) . This implies the curvature of \( \bar{U} \) at \( {y}_{\infty } \) is nonnegative in the Alexandrov sense. It is a basic result in Alexandrov space theory (see for example Theorem 10.9.3 and Corollary 10.9.5 of [9]) that there exists a three-dimensional tangent cone \( {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{U} \) at \( {y}_{\infty } \) which is a metric cone. It is clear that its aperture is \( \leq  {10\varepsilon } \) , thus the tangent cone is nonflat.

Pick a point \( p \in  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{U} \) such that the distance from the vertex \( {y}_{\infty } \) to \( p \) is one and it is nonflat around \( p \) . Then the ball \( B\left( {p,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{U} \) is the Gromov-Hausdorff limit of the scalings of a sequence of balls \( {B}_{0}\left( {{p}_{k},{s}_{k}}\right)  \subset  \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\right) \) by some factors \( {a}_{k} \) , where \( {s}_{k} \rightarrow  {0}^{ + } \) . Since the tangent cone is three-dimensional and nonflat around \( p \) , the factors \( {a}_{k} \) must be comparable with \( {\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {{p}_{k},0}\right) \) . By using the local curvature estimate in Lemma 7.1.2, we actually have the convergence in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology for the solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) on the balls \( {B}_{0}\left( {{p}_{k},{s}_{k}}\right) \) and over some time interval \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {-\delta ,0}\right\rbrack \) for some sufficiently small \( \delta  > 0 \) . The limiting ball \( B\left( {p,\frac{1}{2}}\right)  \subset  {C}_{{y}_{\infty }}\bar{U} \) is a piece of the nonnegative curved and nonflat metric cone whose radial directions are all Ricci flat. On the other hand, by applying Hamilton's strong maximum principle to the evolution equation of the Ricci curvature tensor as in the proof of Lemma 6.3.1, the limiting ball \( B\left( {p,\frac{1}{2}}\right) \) would split off all radial directions isometrically (and locally). Since the limit is nonflat around \( p \) , this is impossible. Therefore we have proved that the curvatures of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) at the new times \( t = 0 \) (corresponding to the original times \( {t}_{k} \) ) stay uniformly bounded at bounded distances from \( {x}_{k} \) for all \( k \) .

We have proved that for each \( A <  + \infty \) , the curvature of the marked manifold \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) at each point \( y \in  {M}_{k} \) with distance from \( {x}_{k} \) at most \( A \) is bounded by \( C\left( A\right) \) . Lemma 7.1.2 extends this curvature control to a backward parabolic neighborhood centered at \( y \) whose radius depends only on the distance from \( y \) to \( {x}_{k} \) . Thus by Shi's local derivative estimates (Theorem 1.4.2) we can control all derivatives of the curvature in such backward parabolic neighborhoods. Then by using the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing and Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5), we can take a \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) subsequent limit to obtain \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) , which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales and is defined on a space-time open subset of \( {M}_{\infty } \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) containing the time slice \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \{ 0\} \) . Clearly it follows from the pinching estimate (7.1.1) that the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator (and hence nonnegative sectional curvature).

Step 3. We further claim that the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) at the time slice \( \{ t = 0\} \) has bounded curvature.

We know that the sectional curvature of the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) is nonnegative everywhere. Argue by contradiction. Suppose the curvature of \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) is not bounded, then by Lemma 6.1.4, there exists a sequence of points \( {q}_{j} \in  {M}_{\infty } \) diverging to infinity such that their scalar curvatures \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{j},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) as \( j \rightarrow   + \infty \)

and

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{j},0}\right)
\]

for \( x \in  B\left( {{q}_{j}, j/\sqrt{{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{j},0}\right) }}\right)  \subset  \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\right) \) . By combining with Lemma 7.1.2 and the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, a subsequence of the rescaled and marked manifolds \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{q}_{j},0}\right) {\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{q}_{j}}\right) \) converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a smooth nonflat limit \( Y \) . By Proposition 6.1.2, the new limit \( Y \) is isometric to a metric product \( N \times  \mathbb{R} \) for some two-dimensional manifold \( N \) . On the other hand, in view of the choice of the points \( \left( {{x}_{k},{t}_{k}}\right) \) , the original limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) ,{x}_{\infty }}\right) \) at the point \( {q}_{j} \) has a canonical neighborhood which is either a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck, a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -cap, or a compact manifold (without boundary) diffeomorphic to a metric quotient of the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) . It follows that for \( j \) large enough, \( {q}_{j} \) is the center of a \( {2\varepsilon } \) -neck of radius \( {\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{j},0\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) . Without loss of generality, we may further assume that \( {2\varepsilon } < {\varepsilon }_{0} \) , where \( {\varepsilon }_{0} \) is the positive constant given in Proposition 6.1.1. Since \( {\left( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {q}_{j},0\right) \right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \rightarrow  0 \) as \( j \rightarrow   + \infty \) , this contradicts Proposition 6.1.1. So the curvature of \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot ,0}\right) }\right) \) is bounded.

Step 4. Finally we want to extend the limit backwards in time to \( - \infty \) .

By Lemma 7.1.2 again, we now know that the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is defined on a backward time interval \( \left\lbrack  {-a,0}\right\rbrack \) for some \( a > 0 \) .

Denote by

\( {t}^{\prime } = \inf \{ \widetilde{t} \mid \) we can take a smooth limit on \( (\widetilde{t},0\rbrack \) (with bounded curvature at each time slice) from a subsequence of the convergent rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k} \) \}.

We first claim that there is a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k} \) which converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a smooth limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) on the maximal time interval \( \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) .

Indeed, let \( {t}_{k}^{\prime } \) be a sequence of negative numbers such that \( {t}_{k}^{\prime } \rightarrow  {t}^{\prime } \) and there exist smooth limits \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) defined on \( \left( {{t}_{k}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . For each \( k \) , the limit has nonnegative sectional curvature and has bounded curvature at each time slice. Moreover by Lemma 7.1.2, the limit has bounded curvature on each subinterval \( \left\lbrack  {-b,0}\right\rbrack   \subset  \left( {{t}_{k}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . Denote by \( \widetilde{Q} \) the scalar curvature upper bound of the limit at time zero (where \( \widetilde{Q} \) is the same for all \( k \) ). Then we can apply the Li-Yau-Hamilton estimate (Corollary 2.5.7) to get

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }^{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{Q}\left( \frac{-{t}_{k}^{\prime }}{t - {t}_{k}^{\prime }}\right) ,
\]

where \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }^{k}\left( {x, t}\right) \) are the scalar curvatures of the limits \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }^{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) . Hence by the definition of convergence and the above curvature estimates, we can find a subsequence of the above convergent rescaled solutions \( {\widetilde{g}}_{k} \) which converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a smooth limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) on the maximal time interval \( \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) .

We next claim that \( {t}^{\prime } =  - \infty \) .

Suppose not, then by Lemma 7.1.2, the curvature of the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) becomes unbounded as \( t \rightarrow  {t}^{\prime } >  - \infty \) . By applying the maximum principle to the evolution equation of the scalar curvature, we see that the infimum of the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time. Note that \( {\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{x}_{\infty },0}\right)  = 1 \) . Thus there exists some point \( {y}_{\infty } \in  {M}_{\infty } \) such that

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{10}}\right)  < \frac{3}{2}
\]

where \( c > 0 \) is the universal constant in Lemma 7.1.2. By using Lemma 7.1.2 again we see that the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) in a small neighborhood of the point \( \left( {{y}_{\infty },{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{10}}\right) \) extends backwards to the time interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{c}{10},{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . We remark that the distances at time \( t \) and time 0 are roughly equivalent in the following sense

(7.1.3)

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  \geq  {d}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  \geq  {d}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  - \text{ const. }
\]

for any \( x, y \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . Indeed from the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.7) we have the estimate

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{Q}\left( \frac{-{t}^{\prime }}{t - {t}^{\prime }}\right) ,\;\text{ on }{M}_{\infty } \times  \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack  .
\]

By applying Lemma 3.4.1 (ii), we have

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  \leq  {d}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)  + {30}\left( {-{t}^{\prime }}\right) \sqrt{\widetilde{Q}}
\]

for any \( x, y \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . On the other hand, since the curvature of the limit metric \( {\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) \) is nonnegative, we have

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {x, y}\right)  \geq  {d}_{0}\left( {x, y}\right)
\]

for any \( x, y \in  {M}_{\infty } \) and \( t \in  \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . Thus we obtain the estimate (7.1.3).

Let us still denote by \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) the subsequence which converges on the maximal time interval \( \left( {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . Consider the rescaled sequence \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) with the marked points \( {x}_{k} \) replaced by the associated sequence of points \( {y}_{k} \rightarrow  {y}_{\infty } \) and the (original unshifted) times \( {t}_{k} \) replaced by any \( {s}_{k} \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{c}{20}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1},{t}_{k} + \left( {{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{20}}\right) {Q}_{k}^{-1}}\right\rbrack \) . It follows from Lemma 7.1.2 that for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) at \( {y}_{k} \) satisfy

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {{y}_{k}, t}\right)  \leq  {10}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{c}{10},{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{10}}\right\rbrack \) . By applying the same arguments as in the above Step 2, we conclude that for any \( A > 0 \) , there is a positive constant \( C\left( A\right)  <  + \infty \) such that

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  C\left( A\right)
\]

for all \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) with \( {d}_{t}\left( {x,{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  A \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{c}{20},{t}^{\prime } + \frac{c}{20}}\right\rbrack \) . The estimate (7.1.3) implies that there is a positive constant \( {A}_{0} \) such that for arbitrarily given small \( {\epsilon }^{\prime } \in  \left( {0,\frac{c}{100}}\right) \) , for \( k \) large enough, there hold

\[
{d}_{t}\left( {{x}_{k},{y}_{k}}\right)  \leq  {A}_{0}
\]

for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } + {\epsilon }^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . By combining with Lemma 7.1.2, we then conclude that for any \( A > 0 \) , there is a positive constant \( \widetilde{C}\left( A\right) \) such that for \( k \) large enough, the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) satisfy

\[
{\widetilde{R}}_{k}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{C}\left( A\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {\widetilde{B}}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k}, A}\right) \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime } - \frac{c}{100}{\left( C\left( A\right) \right) }^{-1},0}\right\rbrack \) .

Now, by taking convergent subsequences from the (original) rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) , we see that the limiting solution \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) is defined on a spacetime open subset of \( {M}_{\infty } \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) containing \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . By repeating the argument of Step 3 and using Lemma 7.1.2, we further conclude the limit \( \left( {{M}_{\infty },{\widetilde{g}}_{\infty }\left( {\cdot , t}\right) }\right) \) has uniformly bounded curvature on \( {M}_{\infty } \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}^{\prime },0}\right\rbrack \) . This is a contradiction.

Therefore we have proved a subsequence of the rescaled solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{\widetilde{g}}_{k}\left( {\cdot , t}\right) ,{x}_{k}}\right) \) converges to an orientable ancient \( \kappa \) -solution, which gives the desired contradiction. This completes the proof of the theorem. 0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: (cf. Theorem I.12.1) Given \( \epsilon ,\kappa ,\sigma  > 0 \) and a function \( \Phi \) as above, one can find \( {r}_{0} > 0 \) with the following property. Let \( g\left( \cdot \right) \) be a Ricci flow solution on a three-manifold \( M \) , defined for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) with \( T \geq  1 \) . We suppose that for each \( t, g\left( t\right) \) is complete, and the sectional curvature is bounded on compact time intervals. Suppose that the Ricci flow has \( \Phi \) -almost nonnegative curvature and is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on scales less than \( \sigma \) . Then for any point \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with \( {t}_{0} \geq  1 \) and \( Q = R\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  \geq  {r}_{0}^{-2} \) , the solution in \( \left\{  {\left( {x, t}\right)  : {\operatorname{dist}}_{{t}_{0}}^{2}\left( {x,{x}_{0}}\right)  < {\left( \epsilon Q\right) }^{-1},{t}_{0} - {\left( \epsilon Q\right) }^{-1} \leq  t \leq  {t}_{0}}\right\} \) is, after scaling by the factor \( Q \) , \( \epsilon \) -close to the corresponding subset of a \( \kappa \) -solution.
